question: According to press reports1, several motorway concessionaire companies, including those controlled by ASTM Group, one of which is SALT SpA operating the A15 motorway (also known as Autostrada della Cisa), sent the MIT2 the new economic and financial plans (known by the acronym ‘PEF’ in Italian).

The PEFs were allegedly pre-notified to the European Commission and envisaged, inter alia, multiannual extensions of motorway concessions. The A15 concession has historically been connected with the construction of the TyrrhenianBrenner multi-modal corridor (Ti-Bre), which has not yet been completed, to link the A15 motorway with the A22 Brenner motorway3.

This project has already been the subject of an EU infringement procedure (2006/4419), which was closed in 2009 with an agreement between the Italian Government and the European Commission laying down precise obligations for the company that received the motorway concession extension without a public tender. In the light of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the facts set out above and does it intend to provide information on the pre-notified documents concerning SALT SpA and the extension of the A15 motorway concession?

What steps could it take, in light of the agreement signed by the Italian Government and the European Commission in 2009, to avoid the risk of circumventions of the obligation to launch a public tender procedure for motorway concessions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.7.2026) The Commission has not received a pre-notification for this specific case and therefore cannot provide further information. It is the responsibility of the Member States to assess whether a planned measure, such as a proposed prolongation of highway concessions, constitutes State aid and, if necessary, to notify the Commission accordingly.
The Commission remains available to support national authorities in ensuring full compliance with relevant EU law and, where needed, will undertake any appropriate measure in this respect.
